## Toronto Vegetarian Dinner Booking Plan for 6
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

For **2026-09-12, 19:00–21:30** in Toronto, the best strategy is to target a **quiet, mid-range vegetarian-friendly restaurant** with **clear vegan dishes**, **wheelchair access**, and **allergen-aware service**. Your budget target of **CAD 45 per person before tax and tip** means you should aim for a menu price ceiling of about **CAD 30–35 per person** to leave room for tax and gratuity.

## Booking Criteria to Use
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check2-square.svg

- **Group size and timing:** confirm a table for **6 people** between **7:00 PM and 9:30 PM**; ask for the quietest available seating.
- **Noise level:** request a **low-noise section** away from bar service, speakers, kitchen, or patio doors.
- **Vegetarian + vegan coverage:** look for a menu with **at least 4–6 clearly labeled vegan entrées or substantial mains**.
- **Nut allergy handling:** ask whether the kitchen can **avoid cross-contact** and whether any dishes or sauces contain nuts, nut oils, or shared garnishes.
- **Accessibility:** confirm **step-free entrance, accessible washroom, and enough space for a wheelchair at the table**.
- **Budget fit:** check whether the menu has **mains in the CAD 18–28 range** and whether shared starters can keep the total under budget.
- **Reservation policy:** ask if they can note **quiet seating + allergy + accessibility** on the booking and whether they can preassign the table.
- **Service style:** choose places that are comfortable with **special requests stated in advance**, not only on arrival.

## Booking Shortlist for the Restaurant
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/list-check.svg

- **Quiet seating request:** “Please place us in the quietest possible section.”
- **Vegan menu check:** “Do you have several vegan mains or can you adapt vegetarian dishes?”
- **Nut allergy note:** “One guest has a nut allergy; can you confirm safe options and cross-contact precautions?”
- **Wheelchair access:** “Is the entrance, table area, and washroom wheelchair accessible?”
- **Price check:** “Can we keep the average spend to about CAD 45 per person before tax and tip?”
- **Reservation note:** “Please add these notes to the booking so the host and kitchen can see them in advance.”

## Sample Message to Send
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/chat-square-text.svg

Hello, I’d like to make a reservation for **6 people** on **Saturday, September 12, 2026**, between **7:00 PM and 9:30 PM**.

We are looking for a **quiet table**, ideally in a low-noise area. We need **good vegetarian and vegan options**, and one guest has a **nut allergy**. Could you please confirm whether your kitchen can accommodate this safely and whether you can note any cross-contact precautions?

We also need **wheelchair access** for one guest, including a step-free path to the table and accessible washroom if available.

Our target budget is **about CAD 45 per person before tax and tip**. If possible, please let us know which menu items would best fit that range.

Thank you — please include these notes with the reservation.

## Best Booking Tactics

- Book **early in the evening** rather than late, since quieter rooms are easier to secure.
- Call or message the restaurant directly instead of relying only on app notes.
- Ask for **written confirmation** of allergy handling and accessibility details.
- If the first choice is uncertain, keep a backup restaurant with the same criteria.

## Sources
- Toronto accessibility and transit planning context: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/streets-parking-transportation/accessible-transportation/
- Canadian food allergy guidance: https://food-guide.canada.ca/en/tips-for-healthy-eating/food-safety/
- General restaurant reservation etiquette and special requests: https://www.opentable.com/restaurant-solutions/resources/restaurant-reservations/
